## q24 (dictionary, medium)

**What are the 2 most common primary diagnoses (the diagnosis listed first for an admission)? Give the description and number of admissions.**

*Trap:* Primary diagnosis is seq_num = 1. The top 2 are tied (7 each), so order is not compared; ranks 3-6 are tied, so the question stops at 2.

```sql
SELECT x.long_title, COUNT(*) AS admissions
FROM diagnoses_icd d JOIN d_icd_diagnoses x ON d.icd_code = x.icd_code AND d.icd_version = x.icd_version
WHERE d.seq_num = 1 GROUP BY x.long_title ORDER BY admissions DESC, x.long_title LIMIT 2
```

| long_title                                         |   admissions |
|:---------------------------------------------------|-------------:|
| Acute kidney failure, unspecified                  |            7 |
| Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery |            7 |

## q43 (multi_step, hard)

**How many patients had both a diabetes diagnosis and a heart failure diagnosis (based on diagnosis descriptions containing 'diabetes' and 'heart failure'), at any time?**

```sql
WITH dx AS (
  SELECT d.subject_id, x.long_title
  FROM diagnoses_icd d JOIN d_icd_diagnoses x ON d.icd_code = x.icd_code AND d.icd_version = x.icd_version)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS patients FROM (
  SELECT subject_id FROM dx GROUP BY subject_id
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN long_title ILIKE '%diabetes%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
     AND SUM(CASE WHEN long_title ILIKE '%heart failure%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0)
```

|   patients |
|-----------:|
|         11 |

## q44 (multi_step, hard)

**Compare the average hospital length of stay in days (rounded to two decimals) for admissions with a sepsis diagnosis versus admissions without one. Return a column has_sepsis with values 'yes' and 'no', and the average.**

```sql
WITH sepsis AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.hadm_id
  FROM diagnoses_icd d JOIN d_icd_diagnoses x ON d.icd_code = x.icd_code AND d.icd_version = x.icd_version
  WHERE x.long_title ILIKE '%sepsis%')
SELECT CASE WHEN s.hadm_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS has_sepsis,
       ROUND(AVG(epoch(a.dischtime - a.admittime) / 86400.0), 2) AS avg_los_days
FROM admissions a LEFT JOIN sepsis s ON a.hadm_id = s.hadm_id
GROUP BY 1
```

| has_sepsis   |   avg_los_days |
|:-------------|---------------:|
| yes          |          13.34 |
| no           |           6.26 |

## q45 (multi_step, hard)

**How many hospital admissions were followed by another admission of the same patient within 30 days of discharge?**

*Trap:* Needs a window function or self-join over each patient's admissions.

```sql
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT subject_id, hadm_id, dischtime,
         LEAD(admittime) OVER (PARTITION BY subject_id ORDER BY admittime) AS next_admit
  FROM admissions)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS admissions_readmitted_30d FROM ordered
WHERE next_admit IS NOT NULL AND next_admit <= dischtime + INTERVAL 30 DAY
```

|   admissions_readmitted_30d |
|----------------------------:|
|                          53 |

## q49 (multi_step, hard)

**For the 3 races with the most admissions (using the race value exactly as recorded), what is the average hospital length of stay in days? Round to two decimals.**

```sql
WITH top_race AS (
  SELECT race FROM admissions GROUP BY race ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3)
SELECT a.race, ROUND(AVG(epoch(a.dischtime - a.admittime) / 86400.0), 2) AS avg_los_days
FROM admissions a JOIN top_race t ON a.race = t.race GROUP BY a.race
```

| race                   |   avg_los_days |
|:-----------------------|---------------:|
| WHITE                  |           7.04 |
| UNKNOWN                |           9.49 |
| BLACK/AFRICAN AMERICAN |           6.11 |
